declarations.name: buildBarTable
declarations.description:
Builds the table fallback: one row per category, one column per series.

A `[min, max]` floating-bar tuple renders as a single cell formatted
`"min – max"` (en dash), keeping one column per series rather than
doubling the column count only for series that use tuples.

Bar chart for series plotted against shared categories.

The component takes semantic categories and series and owns its renderer.
It exposes no engine selector and no universal native configuration; the
rendering engine is an implementation detail apart from the documented
unsafe escape hatch.
declarations.name: KDChartBar

members.name: _frameTooltip
members.description: Active frame-managed hover tooltip, or null when hidden.

members.name: hostSize
members.description:
Measured renderer host size, or null before the first measurement. Models
that depend on available room read this so the renderer and any component
chrome decide from the same numbers.

members.name: captionText
members.description: Optional short summary rendered beneath the chart.

members.name: renderHostOverlay
members.description:
Optional chrome layered over the renderer host, for chart-specific UI that
has to sit outside the renderer's DOM. The frame positions the layer and
keeps it out of the renderer's subtree; what goes in it is up to the
component, and the frame stays engine neutral either way.

members.name: formatInteractionTooltip
members.description:
Formats hover tooltip content for frame-managed renderers. Return null to
suppress the tooltip for a given interaction.

members.name: capabilities
members.description:
Capabilities are constant per renderer class, so they are read from a
throwaway instance during the first render. Reading them after mount would
mean changing state inside an update cycle.

members.name: unsafeGetNativeInstance
members.description:
Unstable escape hatch returning the underlying engine instance, or null
when nothing is mounted. The type is engine-specific and may change or be
removed without a breaking-change release.

members.name: refresh
members.description: Forces a renderer update, e.g. after mutating a model array in place.

members.name: unmountRenderer
members.description: Drops the live renderer when there is nothing left to draw.

members.name: clearEmptyModel
members.description: Clears renderer and table view when the semantic model is empty.

members.name: recordHostSize
members.description:
Resize observations arrive outside Lit's update cycle, so recording them as
state schedules a normal re-render. Identical sizes are dropped to keep
engine reflows from turning into a render loop.

declarations.description:
Sunburst chart for hierarchical part-to-whole data.

The component takes a semantic hierarchy and owns its renderer. It exposes no
engine selector and no universal native configuration; the rendering engine
is an implementation detail apart from the documented unsafe escape hatch.

members.description: Builds the renderer model, or null when there is nothing to draw.

members.name: labelMetrics
members.description:
The chart fills the largest square its host allows, so its radius is half
the shorter side. Carrying this on the model is what keeps the renderer's
label suppression and the overlay below in agreement.

members.name: buildTableView
members.description: Builds the tabular fallback, which is also the CSV source of truth.

members.name: renderHostOverlay
members.description:
Labels that do not fit their sector are not painted by the chart. They are
drawn here instead, as Lit owned anchors that reveal the full label and
value through the Shidoka tooltip. The chart never sees this DOM and the
anchors disappear with the template, so there is nothing to unbind.

The chart tooltip skips overlay-owned sectors in this mode, so these
anchors are the hover detail source for truncated and marker labels.

`assistiveText` is deliberately emptied. The tooltip puts it on both the
`aria-label` and the native `title` of its anchor button, and it defaults
to `'Tooltip'`, so leaving it alone paints a second browser-rendered
tooltip and hides the real label from assistive technology. With it empty,
the anchor takes its name from the slotted content and the tooltip's own
`aria-describedby` still points at the visible text.

declarations.name: LABEL_FONT_SIZE_PX
declarations.description: Font size the renderer draws segment labels with.

declarations.name: DEFAULT_LABEL_METRICS
declarations.description:
Metrics used until the host has been measured, for example on a server or
during the first paint. This is the radius of a square the size of the
frame's default height, and the first resize observation replaces it.

declarations.name: OUTER_RADIUS_FRACTION
declarations.description: Outer radius used by the generated option, as a fraction of the radius box.

declarations.name: estimateTextWidthPx
declarations.description:
Rendered width of a run of text, estimated the way the planner budgets for
it. Exposed so callers and tests can check a planned label against the room
its sector reported.

declarations.name: estimateChipWidthPx
declarations.description: Rendered width of an overlay pill, which is its text plus its own chrome.

declarations.name: placementFootprintPx
declarations.description:
How much of its ring's arc a label takes up, in pixels.

A drawn label runs outwards along its radius, so what it spends on the arc is
one line of text. A pill lies level, so it spends its width where it lies
along the arc and its height where it lies across the ring, the same
projection that sized it in the first place. A marker is a circle, so it
spends its diameter whichever way it is approached.

declarations.name: placementClearancePx
declarations.description:
Clear space between two labels on the same ring, in pixels along the arc.
Negative once they overlap.

declarations.name: ringThicknessPx
declarations.description:
Thickness of one ring in pixels, which is all the room a label the chart
draws itself has along its own radius. Every ring is equally thick, so this
is one number for the whole chart.

Exported so the renderer can cap the labels it paints at the same figure the
planner budgeted them against. The planner works from an average glyph
advance, so a label of unusually wide glyphs could still measure a little
over its budget once the browser lays it out; the renderer's cap is what
turns that into an ellipsis instead of a label crossing its ring boundary.

declarations.name: planSunburstLabels
declarations.description:
Plans one placement per node.

`display` answers whether the chart can draw the label itself, which it only
does along the ring and only within it: `inline` when one line of the full
label is no longer than the ring is thick, `truncated` when the overlay has
to take over, and `marker` when not even a level pill has room for readable
text.

For the placements the overlay takes over, `text` and `chipCapacityPx` come
from the pill measurement instead, so the text is cut to the room the pill
really has. A pill is often roomy enough to show a label in full even though
the chart could not draw it, because a pill lying along a broad arc has the
whole chord to spend where a drawn label only ever has its ring.

A label sized against its own sector can still land on top of its neighbour,
so a second pass walks each ring and reduces the smaller of any two colliding
labels to a marker. That runs last, which is why `display` here is the final
answer for both the overlay and the chart's own suppression.

`metrics` describes the drawn size of the chart. Callers that have not
measured the host yet can omit it and get the documented default.

declarations.name: constrainedPlacements
declarations.description: Placements whose label does not fit and therefore need a tooltip anchor.

declarations.name: placementPosition
declarations.description:
Position of a placement inside a square overlay that matches the chart's
radius box, expressed in percent so no pixel measurement is needed.

declarations.name: labelPathKey
declarations.description:
Lookup key for a node path. Uses a unit separator so labels containing
ordinary punctuation cannot collide.

declarations.name: suppressedLabelKeys
declarations.description: Paths whose chart-drawn label must be suppressed.

declarations.name: selectionFromPlacement
declarations.description: Normalized selection payload for a constrained overlay anchor.

declarations.name: nodeTotal
declarations.description: Sum of a node's own value or of its descendants.

declarations.name: hierarchyTotal
declarations.description: Sum across every top level node.

declarations.name: hierarchyDepth
declarations.description: Depth of the deepest branch, where a flat list of nodes has depth 1.

declarations.name: flattenHierarchy
declarations.description: Flattens the hierarchy into leaf paths, outermost ancestor first.

declarations.name: buildSunburstTable
declarations.description:
Builds the table fallback. One column per hierarchy level plus a value
column, so the CSV export mirrors what is on screen.

declarations.description:
Engine-neutral chrome shared by hybrid chart components.

The frame owns the header, controls, table fallback, CSV export, theme
observation, resize coordination and normalized events. It knows nothing
about any charting engine: everything engine-specific reaches it through
`ChartRenderer` and `RendererCapabilities`.
